facts.text: Rolla is named after Rollie Ray Williamson, who arrived in Western Kansas in 1907 in a covered wagon with his mother and uncle to meet his father.
During the Civil War, Rolla hosted the southwest branch of the Pacific Railroad, and later celebrated the opening of Route 66 in Missouri.
Rolla sits in the south-central Ozarks Highland and is home to Missouri University of Science and Technology, a university founded before the Civil War.
The 1930s Dust Bowl hit Rolla hard, amplifying the Great Depression’s economic blow to the area.
Rolla was officially laid out in 1913, following the establishment of its post office in 1907.
Rolla consistently ranks among the country’s most livable communities, according to several publications.
